scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported c. 1530–1715 interval is map coverage, not the viceroyalty’s 1535–1821 historical duration. The polygon is not a certified rendering of every territory across that duration.

A colonial jurisdiction extended beyond modern Mexico but local lives varied enormously. Source examples are tied to specific cities, schools, kitchens or archives, not universalized. Narrative awaits independent review.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Viceroyalty of New Spain was established in 1535 and ruled from Mexico City until independence in 1821. Its historic jurisdiction included much more than modern Mexico; the imported polygon covers only about 1530 to 1715 and is not a complete border history. Indigenous, African, Spanish and mixed communities lived under unequal colonial laws while making their own families, art, petitions, foods and languages. Silver linked Acapulco to Asia, and Indigenous knowledge shaped medicine. Mexico inherited most, but not all, of the viceroyalty in 1821.
